title: JO6 11 10 sweet potato (VSU Yellow): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: JO6 11 10 sweet potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: JO6 11 10 sweet potato is a sweet potato variety from PhilRootcrops, VSU. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: JO6 11 10 is a registered sweet potato variety, also sold or known as VSU Yellow or NSIC Sp 33. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2011 as NSIC 2011 Sp 33. It comes from PhilRootcrops, VSU. Its record notes 16.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where JO6 11 10 sweet potato is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for VSU Yellow or NSIC Sp 33, this is the same sweet potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [sweet potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/sweet-potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 16.9 t/ha beats the average of its group, 15.15. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit sweet potato fields most often: [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have yellow orange flesh and pink skin. Dry matter is 41.1 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 29.6 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pink skin, yellow orange flesh, ovate roots, high dry matter.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: topped all entries (9.58 t/ha) in a PhilRootcrops regional yield trial and gave more flour per hectare than native cultivars. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant JO6 11 10 sweet potato
Pick by use and market: yellow or orange flesh for snacks and fries, purple for processing, white for boiling. Weevils are the main enemy, so plant clean cuttings and harvest on time.

items.q: Is VSU Yellow the same as JO6 11 10?
items.a: Yes. VSU Yellow is another name for JO6 11 10, registered as NSIC 2011 Sp 33. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 16.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of JO6 11 10?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
